verdict.rationale: Bevy is free, open-source software under MIT or Apache 2.0 and is consumed as a normal Rust dependency. Its source is on GitHub and its crate is on crates.io, so the entire engine runs on the user's own machines with no vendor-hosted service involved. A runtime probe confirms the crate resolves on crates.io with the MIT OR Apache-2.0 license, and community comments praise the no-strings licensing. Missing for 10: explicit first-party documentation framing local, vendor-independent operation (e.g. building from source) as a self-hosting guide.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: It is free and open-source forever under your choice of the MIT or Apache 2.0 licenses.
Bevy is just a normal Rust dependency. You can either add it to an existing Rust project or create a new one.
The code is free and open-source because we believe developers should fully own their tools.
